title: A formally unramified ring map has a universal first order thickening (algebra)
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings which is formally unramified: for every $R$-algebra $A$, every ideal $I\subseteq A$ with $I^2=0$ and every $R$-algebra map $a:S\to A/I$ there is at most one $R$-algebra map $a':S\to A$ with $q\circ a'=a$, where $q:A\to A/I$ is the quotient map. Then there exist an $R$-algebra $S'$ and a surjective $R$-algebra map $\pi:S'\to S$ whose kernel $K$ satisfies $K^2=0$, with the following universal property: for every $R$-algebra $A$, every ideal $I\subseteq A$ with $I^2=0$ (quotient map $q:A\to A/I$) and every $R$-algebra map $a:S\to A/I$, there is exactly one $R$-algebra map $a':S'\to A$ with $q\circ a'=a\circ\pi$. The pair $(S',\pi)$ is unique up to unique isomorphism of $R$-algebras compatible with the maps to $S$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 04EB (label lemma-universal-thickening, in Section 04EA 'Conormal modules and universal thickenings', section-conormal), with the uniqueness remark following it; formally unramified as in Algebra, Definition 00UN (definition-formally-unramified); the proof uses Lemma 00UO (lemma-characterize-formally-unramified: equivalent to Omega_{S/R}=0)

proof.text: *Presentation.* Choose a family $(z_t)_{t\in T}$ of generators of $S$ as an $R$-algebra (for instance $T=S$, $z_s=s$). Let $P=R[x_t:t\in T]$ be the polynomial ring [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] and $p:P\to S$ the $R$-algebra map with $p(x_t)=z_t$ (its universal property). The image of $p$ is an $R$-subalgebra of $S$ containing all $z_t$, so $p$ is surjective. Put $J=\ker p$; $p$ induces an isomorphism of $R$-algebras $P/J\cong S$, through which we identify $S=P/J$. The $P$-modules $J/J^2$ and $S\otimes_P M$ ($M$ a $P$-module) are killed by $J$, hence are $S$-modules, and $P$-linear maps between such modules are $S$-linear.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 04EB (label lemma-universal-thickening, line 40920), first three sentences ('Choose a set of generators z_i ... Let J = Ker(P -> S)')

proof.text: *The map $\mathrm d:J/J^2\to S\otimes_P\Omega_{P/R}$ is surjective.* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-differential-maps] with $(A,B,\mathfrak a,C)=(R,P,J,S)$: there are maps $J/J^2\xrightarrow{\delta}S\otimes_P\Omega_{P/R}\xrightarrow{w}\Omega_{S/R}$, $\delta(g\bmod J^2)=1\otimes\mathrm dg$, $w(s\otimes\mathrm dg)=s\,\mathrm d(p(g))$, $\delta$ $P$-linear (hence $S$-linear, step 1), with $\operatorname{im}\delta=\ker w$. Since $R\to S$ is formally unramified, $\Omega_{S/R}=0$ by (1)$\Rightarrow$(2) of [lem-weil-pbc-formally-unramified-ring-iff-kahler-zero] (its condition (1) is the hypothesis of the statement verbatim). Hence $\ker w=S\otimes_P\Omega_{P/R}$ and $\delta$ is surjective.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 04EB (label lemma-universal-thickening, line 40920), fourth sentence and display ('Consider the map d : J/J^2 -> Omega_{P/R} (x)_P S, see Lemma 00RU (lemma-differential-seq). This is surjective since Omega_{S/R} = 0 by assumption, see Lemma 00UO (lemma-characterize-formally-unramified)'); tags verified: 00RU,algebra-lemma-differential-seq; 00UO,algebra-lemma-characterize-formally-unramified

proof.text: *Splitting and the ideal $J'$.* By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis-any-variables], $S\otimes_P\Omega_{P/R}$ is a free $S$-module with basis $e_t=1\otimes\mathrm dx_t$, $t\in T$. By step 2 choose $g_t\in J$ with $\delta(g_t\bmod J^2)=e_t$, and let $\sigma:S\otimes_P\Omega_{P/R}\to J/J^2$ be the $S$-linear map with $\sigma(e_t)=g_t\bmod J^2$ (a free module). Then $\delta\circ\sigma=\mathrm{id}$ (it holds on the basis), so $J/J^2=\ker\delta\oplus\operatorname{im}\sigma$ as $S$-modules, $\sigma$ is injective, and the restriction $\delta':=\delta|_{\operatorname{im}\sigma}:\operatorname{im}\sigma\to S\otimes_P\Omega_{P/R}$ is an isomorphism with inverse $\sigma$. Let $J'=\{g\in J: g\bmod J^2\in\operatorname{im}\sigma\}$, the preimage of the $P$-submodule $\operatorname{im}\sigma$ under the $P$-linear map $J\to J/J^2$; it is a $P$-submodule of $P$, i.e. an ideal, with $J^2\subseteq J'\subseteq J$ and $J'/J^2=\operatorname{im}\sigma$. So $\delta':J'/J^2\to S\otimes_P\Omega_{P/R}$, $g\bmod J^2\mapsto 1\otimes\mathrm dg$, is an isomorphism of $S$-modules.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 04EB (label lemma-universal-thickening, line 40920), fifth to seventh sentences ('Note that Omega_{P/R} is free on dx_i ... we may choose a splitting ... Let J^2 ⊂ J' ⊂ J be the ideal of P such that J'/J^2 is the second summand'); Lemma 00RX (lemma-differentials-polynomial-ring) for the basis, tag verified: 00RX,algebra-lemma-differentials-polynomial-ring

proof.text: *The thickening $S'\to S$.* Put $S'=P/J'$, an $R$-algebra, and let $\pi:S'\to S=P/J$ be the $R$-algebra map induced by $p$ (well defined as $J'\subseteq J$); it is surjective since $p$ is, and $\pi\circ\rho=p$ for the quotient map $\rho:P\to S'$. Its kernel is $K=J/J'$, and $K^2=(J^2+J')/J'=0$ since $J^2\subseteq J'$. (Moreover $K\cong (J/J^2)/(J'/J^2)\cong\ker\delta$, not needed below.)

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 04EB (label lemma-universal-thickening, line 40920), 'Set S' = P/J'. We obtain a short exact sequence 0 -> J/J' -> S' -> S -> 0 and we see that J/J' ≅ K is a square zero ideal in S''

proof.text: *Lifts of $a\circ p$ to $A$ form a torsor under derivations.* Let $A$ be an $R$-algebra with structure map $b:R\to A$, $I\subseteq A$ an ideal with $I^2=0$, $q:A\to A/I$ the quotient map and $a:S\to A/I$ an $R$-algebra map. Since $I^2=0$, $I$ is an $A/I$-module, hence an $S$-module via $a$ and a $P$-module via $a\circ p$; for $h\in A$, $i\in I$ one has $h\,i=q(h)\cdot i$. (a) There is an $R$-algebra map $\beta:P\to A$ with $q\circ\beta=a\circ p$: choose $\beta(x_t)\in A$ with $q(\beta(x_t))=a(z_t)$ ($q$ is surjective) and let $\beta$ be the $R$-algebra map with these values [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]; $q\circ\beta$ and $a\circ p$ are $R$-algebra maps $P\to A/I$ agreeing on every $x_t$, hence equal by the uniqueness in [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Then $\beta(J)\subseteq I$, $\beta(J^2)\subseteq I^2=0$, and $\beta(h)\,i=p(h)\cdot i$ for $h\in P$, $i\in I$. (b) If $D:P\to I$ is an $R$-derivation of $P$ into the $P$-module $I$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], then $\beta+D:P\to A$ is an $R$-algebra map with $q\circ(\beta+D)=a\circ p$: it is additive, $(\beta+D)(fg)=\beta(f)\beta(g)+\beta(f)D(g)+\beta(g)D(f)=(\beta(f)+D(f))(\beta(g)+D(g))-D(f)D(g)$ with $D(f)D(g)\in I^2=0$, and $D$ vanishes on the image of $R$ (so $(\beta+D)(r\cdot1)=b(r)$, and $D(1)=0$); $q\circ D=0$. Conversely, if $\beta':P\to A$ is an $R$-algebra map with $q\circ\beta'=a\circ p$, then $D=\beta'-\beta$ takes values in $I$, vanishes on the image of $R$, and $D(fg)=\beta'(f)\beta'(g)-\beta(f)\beta(g)=D(f)\beta(g)+\beta(f)D(g)+D(f)D(g)$ with $D(f)D(g)=0$, i.e. $D$ is an $R$-derivation $P\to I$. (c) By the universal property in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], $R$-derivations $D:P\to I$ are exactly the maps $\psi\circ\mathrm d$ with $\psi:\Omega_{P/R}\to I$ $P$-linear, $\psi$ unique; since $P$ acts on $I$ through $p$, $P$-linear $\psi$ correspond bijectively to $S$-linear $\varphi:S\otimes_P\Omega_{P/R}\to I$ by $\varphi(s\otimes\omega)=s\,\psi(\omega)$ (extension of scalars). Hence the $R$-algebra maps $\beta':P\to A$ with $q\circ\beta'=a\circ p$ are exactly the maps $\beta_\varphi(g)=\beta(g)+\varphi(1\otimes\mathrm dg)$, for a unique $S$-linear $\varphi:S\otimes_P\Omega_{P/R}\to I$. (In the basis of [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis-any-variables], with $\delta_t=\varphi(e_t)$ and $\mathrm dg=\sum_t\frac{\partial g}{\partial x_t}\mathrm dx_t$, this reads $\beta_\varphi(x_t)=\beta(x_t)+\delta_t$ and $\beta_\varphi(g)=\beta(g)+\sum_t\delta_t\,\beta(\frac{\partial g}{\partial x_t})$, the source's formula.)

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 04EB (label lemma-universal-thickening, line 40920), from 'Namely, let (I ⊂ A, a, b) be an arbitrary diagram. We may choose an R-algebra map beta : P -> A' to the display 'beta'(g) = beta(g) + sum_i delta_i beta(dg/dx_i)'; the source parametrizes the lifts by the delta_i, here by derivations, which is the same parametrization through the basis dx_t

proof.text: *Existence and uniqueness of $a'$.* Keep the data of step 5. Since $\rho:P\to S'$ is surjective with kernel $J'$ and $\pi\circ\rho=p$ (step 4), $a'\mapsto a'\circ\rho$ is a bijection from the $R$-algebra maps $a':S'\to A$ with $q\circ a'=a\circ\pi$ onto the $R$-algebra maps $\beta':P\to A$ with $q\circ\beta'=a\circ p$ and $\beta'(J')=0$. By step 5 (c) the latter are the $\beta_\varphi$ with $\beta_\varphi(J')=0$. Let $\bar\beta:J'/J^2\to I$, $g\bmod J^2\mapsto\beta(g)$: well defined as $\beta(J^2)=0$, and $S$-linear as $\beta(hg)=\beta(h)\beta(g)=p(h)\cdot\beta(g)$ (step 5 (a)). For $g\in J'$, $\varphi(1\otimes\mathrm dg)=\varphi(\delta'(g\bmod J^2))$ with $\delta'$ the isomorphism of step 3 (the map $\delta$ of [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-differential-maps] restricted to $J'/J^2$). So $\beta_\varphi(J')=0$ iff $\bar\beta+\varphi\circ\delta'=0$ on $J'/J^2$, iff $\varphi=-\bar\beta\circ\delta'^{-1}$, as $\delta'$ is an isomorphism. Thus exactly one $\varphi$, hence exactly one $\beta'$ and exactly one $a'$, satisfies the conditions: $(S',\pi)$ has the universal property of the statement.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 04EB (label lemma-universal-thickening, line 40920), last sentences ('Since the map d|_{J'/J^2} : J'/J^2 -> Omega_{P/R} (x)_P S ... is an isomorphism by construction, we see that there is a unique choice of delta_i in I such that beta'(g) = 0 for all g in J' ... The uniqueness of the solution implies the uniqueness required in the lemma')

proof.text: *Uniqueness up to unique isomorphism.* Let $(S'_1,\pi_1)$, $(S'_2,\pi_2)$ both have the properties of the statement, with kernels $K_1,K_2$. Apply the universal property of $(S'_1,\pi_1)$ to $A=S'_2$, $I=K_2$ and $a=\bar\pi_2^{-1}:S\to S'_2/K_2$, the inverse of the isomorphism $\bar\pi_2:S'_2/K_2\to S$ induced by $\pi_2$: the condition $q\circ\phi=a\circ\pi_1$ on an $R$-algebra map $\phi:S'_1\to S'_2$ is $\pi_2\circ\phi=\pi_1$, so there is exactly one such $\phi$. Likewise exactly one $\psi:S'_2\to S'_1$ with $\pi_1\circ\psi=\pi_2$. Then $\psi\circ\phi$ and $\mathrm{id}_{S'_1}$ both satisfy $\pi_1\circ(-)=\pi_1$, so by the uniqueness for $(S'_1,\pi_1)$ applied to $A=S'_1$, $I=K_1$, $a=\bar\pi_1^{-1}$, $\psi\circ\phi=\mathrm{id}$; symmetrically $\phi\circ\psi=\mathrm{id}$. So $\phi$ is the unique isomorphism of $R$-algebras compatible with the maps to $S$.

lean.statement: theorem exists_universalFirstOrderThickening (R S : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [FormallyUnramified R S] : ∃ (S' : Type u) (_ : CommRing S') (_ : Algebra R S') (π : S' →ₐ[R] S), Function.Surjective π ∧ RingHom.ker π.toRingHom ^ 2 = ⊥ ∧ (∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] (I : Ideal A), I ^ 2 = ⊥ → ∀ a : S →ₐ[R] A ⧸ I, ∃! a' : S' →ₐ[R] A, (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R I).comp a' = a.comp π) ∧ (∀ (T : Type u) [CommRing T] [Algebra R T] (πT : T →ₐ[R] S), Function.Surjective πT → RingHom.ker πT.toRingHom ^ 2 = ⊥ → (∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] (I : Ideal A), I ^ 2 = ⊥ → ∀ a : S →ₐ[R] A ⧸ I, ∃! a' : T →ₐ[R] A, (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R I).comp a' = a.comp πT) → ∃! e : S' ≃ₐ[R] T, πT.comp e.toAlgHom = π)
